concepts.name: Constitution, Company rise and the Acts of 1773-1784
concepts.description: What a constitution is and does; the Company's rise to territorial power; the Regulating Act 1773, Amending Act 1781 and Pitt's India Act 1784.
concepts.idea: Early Parliamentary Acts built a central authority over the Company: a Governor-General and Supreme Court in 1773, a corrective Act in 1781 and double government in 1784.
concepts.rule: A constitution (from Latin constituere, to set up) is the master rule-book that structures and limits government. The Company obtained the Diwani of Bengal, Bihar and Odisha in 1765 after Buxar (1764). The Regulating Act 1773 created the Governor-General of Bengal (Warren Hastings), a four-member Executive Council, subordinated Bombay and Madras and set up the Supreme Court at Calcutta (1774; Chief Justice and three judges). The Amending Act 1781 exempted official acts from the Court and sent appeals from Provincial Courts to the Governor-General-in-Council. Pitt's India Act 1784 created the Board of Control, giving double government.
concepts.example: The Board of Control (1784) supervised political affairs while the Court of Directors kept commerce.

questions.q: The word 'constitution' is traced to a Latin verb. Which one of the following best gives the sense of that verb, and hence the original idea of a constitution?
questions.e: The word 'constitution' is commonly traced to the Latin verb constituere, meaning to establish or set up. Also intro treats the Constitution as the framework set up for government.
w: Not the sense of the Latin root; the root verb constituere means to establish.
Counsel-taking is a different Latin root (consulere); the root of constitution is constituere, to set up.
Constare, 'to stand firm', is a different Latin word; the root is constituere.

questions.q: In 1765, after the Battle of Buxar, the Mughal Emperor Shah Alam II granted the East India Company the 'Diwani' of Bengal, Bihar and Odisha. In constitutional terms, this grant is significant because it
questions.a: gave the Company rights over revenue and civil justice and so began its career as a territorial power
o: gave the Company rights over revenue and civil justice and so began its career as a territorial power
made the Company the legal sovereign of the three provinces, answerable only to the Crown
gave the Company the right to maintain an army and conduct foreign relations in the Mughal's name
created the first Governor-General of Bengal with control over the other presidencies
questions.e: Battle of Buxar 1764; Diwani granted by Shah Alam II in 1765; it meant revenue and civil justice rights and started the Company's career as a territorial power. Also.
w: Diwani was a revenue and civil-justice right, not sovereignty; sovereignty over Company territories was asserted only by Parliament later.
Diwani concerned revenue and civil justice, not the army or foreign relations.
The office of Governor-General of Bengal was created by the Regulating Act of 1773, not by the Diwani.

questions.q: The Regulating Act of 1773 provided for a Supreme Court at Calcutta, established in 1774. The Court as originally constituted consisted of
questions.a: a Chief Justice and three other judges
o: a Chief Justice and three other judges
a Chief Justice and five other judges
a Chief Justice and two other judges
four judges, one of whom was the Governor-General
questions.e: The Supreme Court at Calcutta had a Chief Justice and three judges and civil and criminal jurisdiction over British subjects in Bengal. Also.
w: The Act fixed three other judges, not five.
The Act fixed three other judges, not two.
The Governor-General sat on the Executive Council and was not a judge of the Court; the Court had a Chief Justice and three judges.

questions.q: A system in which the commercial affairs of the East India Company were left with its Court of Directors while its political affairs were supervised by a body representing the British Government is called double government. It was introduced by
questions.a: Pitt's India Act of 1784, which created the Board of Control
o: Pitt's India Act of 1784, which created the Board of Control
the Regulating Act of 1773, which created the Executive Council
the Amending Act of 1781, which created the Provincial Courts
the Government of India Act of 1858, which created the Secretary of State
questions.e: Pitt's India Act of 1784 let the Court of Directors manage commercial matters and created the Board of Control for political matters; this is double government (abolished in 1858). The Regulating Act of 1773 and the Amending Act of 1781 preceded it and set up no such parallel controlling body.
w: The 1773 Act created the Governor-General and a four-member Executive Council; no separate body for political affairs.
The 1781 Act corrected jurisdictional defects of the 1773 Act; it did not create a second controlling body.
The 1858 Act abolished the double government; it did not introduce it.

questions.q: A constitution is often called the master rule-book of a political community. Which one of the following best explains how it prevents arbitrary rule?
questions.a: It specifies who decides what and how, so that rulers are bound by procedures and rights
o: It specifies who decides what and how, so that rulers are bound by procedures and rights
It transfers all residual authority to the executive so that quick decisions are possible
It leaves the manner of decision-making to the conventions of each government
It fixes the aspirations of society but leaves the limits on authority to ordinary laws
questions.e: As commonly stated, a constitution specifies who decides what, how decisions are made and under what constraints, which reduces conflict over power and prevents arbitrary rule by binding rulers to procedures and rights.
w: A constitution limits authority; it does not hand all residual power to the executive.
A constitution lays down the decision-making rules; it does not leave them to the ruler's convention.
Limits on authority are themselves a core function of a constitution, not left to ordinary laws.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the functions of a constitution:

1. It organises and structures the organs of government.
2. It distributes powers and functions among the organs of government.
3. It defines the rights and duties of citizens.
4. It sets limits on the authority of the government.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: structuring the organs of government is a listed function. Statement 2 is correct: distribution of powers among the organs is a listed function. Statement 3 is correct: rights and duties of citizens are a listed function. Statement 4 is correct: limiting governmental authority is a listed function.
w: '1, 3 and 4 only' leaves out statement 2, which is correct
'1, 2 and 4 only' leaves out statement 3, which is correct
'1, 2 and 3 only' leaves out statement 4, which is correct

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the meaning and role of a constitution:

1. The word 'constitution' comes from the Latin verb constare, meaning to stand together.
2. It provides a common set of rules that lets individuals and groups live together peacefully and cooperate in social, economic and political life.
3. It deals with the structure of government but leaves the relationship between the state and the people to ordinary law.
4. It gives institutional shape to shared goals such as justice, welfare, equality, security and development while keeping governments accountable.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: it comes from constituere, meaning to establish or set up. Statement 2 is correct: this is the coordination role of a constitution. Statement 3 is incorrect: regulating the relationship between the state and the people is itself a function of a constitution. Statement 4 is correct: this is the enabling-aspirations role.
w: '1 and 4 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct
'3 and 4 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct
'1 and 2 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 4, which is correct

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the rise of the East India Company:

1. The Company obtained the Diwani of Bengal, Bihar and Odisha from the Nawab of Bengal after the Battle of Plassey.
2. The Diwani was the right to collect revenue and to administer civil justice.
3. The grant of Diwani laid the foundation of Company rule as a territorial power in India.
4. The Company traded under a charter granted by Queen Elizabeth I in 1600.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: the Diwani was granted by the Mughal Emperor Shah Alam II in 1765 after the Battle of Buxar (1764), not by the Nawab of Bengal after Plassey. Statement 2 is correct: Diwani meant the right to collect revenue and administer civil justice. Statement 3 is correct: from then the Company was a territorial power, not only a trader. Statement 4 is correct: the Company traded under the charter of Elizabeth I of 1600; the British first arrived in India as traders around 1608. So 2, 3 and 4 only.
w: '1, 2 and 4 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct
'1, 2, 3 and 4' includes statement 1, which is incorrect
'1, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Regulating Act of 1773:

1. It designated the Governor of Bengal as the Governor-General of Bengal, assisted by an Executive Council of four members.
2. It set up a separate legislative council to make laws for Bengal.
3. Bombay and Madras Governors, hitherto independent, were placed under the Governor-General of Bengal.
4. Warren Hastings was the first Governor-General of Bengal.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: this is the central provision. Statement 2 is incorrect: the Act did not create a separate legislative council; legislative functions were separated only by the Charter Act of 1853. Statement 3 is correct: the three presidencies had earlier been independent of one another. Statement 4 is correct: Hastings was the first holder of the post.
w: '1, 2 and 3 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 4, which is correct
'1, 2 and 4 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct
'1, 2, 3 and 4' includes statement 2, which is incorrect

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Regulating Act of 1773:

1. The Supreme Court at Calcutta was established in 1774 under the Act, with a Chief Justice and three other judges.
2. Its civil and criminal jurisdiction extended over British subjects in Bengal.
3. The Court's jurisdiction extended equally over British subjects in the presidencies of Bombay and Madras.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: the Act provided for a Supreme Court at Calcutta (1774) comprising one Chief Justice and three other judges. Statement 2 is correct: this is the jurisdiction given by the Act. Statement 3 is incorrect: the Court at Calcutta had jurisdiction over British subjects in Bengal; Bombay and Madras were not placed under it.
w: '2 and 3 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct
'1, 2 and 3 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect
'2 only' leaves out statement 1, which is correct

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Regulating Act of 1773:

1. Servants of the Company were barred from private trade and from accepting presents or bribes from the natives.
2. It was the first of the Acts by which the British Parliament sought to control the East India Company, coming before Pitt's India Act of 1784.
3. It abolished the Company's trade monopoly in India and opened Indian trade to all British merchants.
4. It treated the Company as a body with political and administrative functions as well as its trading role, a recognition made for the first time.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: the Act prohibited private trade and the acceptance of presents or bribes by Company servants. Statement 2 is correct: it was the first of the Parliamentary Acts to regulate the Company, preceding Pitt's India Act of 1784. Statement 3 is incorrect: the Company's trade monopoly in India was abolished by the Charter Act of 1813, not by the Regulating Act. Statement 4 is correct: the Act recognised, for the first time, the political and administrative functions of the Company. So 1, 2 and 4 only.
w: '1, 2 and 3 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect (the monopoly ended in 1813), and leaves out statement 4, which is correct
'2, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect (the monopoly ended in 1813), and leaves out statement 1, which is correct
'1, 2, 3 and 4' includes statement 3, which is incorrect (the monopoly ended in 1813)

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Amending Act of 1781:

1. The Act of Settlement is another name for the 1781 amendment of the Regulating Act.
2. Acts done by the Governor-General and his Council in an official capacity were placed beyond the Supreme Court's jurisdiction.
3. It excluded revenue matters and matters arising in the collection of revenue from the jurisdiction of the Supreme Court.
4. It provided that appeals from the Provincial Courts would lie to the Supreme Court.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: the Amending Act of 1781 is also called the Act of Settlement. Statement 2 is correct: acts done by the Governor-General and his Council in an official capacity, and by Company servants in their official actions, were exempted from the Supreme Court's jurisdiction. Statement 3 is correct: revenue matters and matters arising in the collection of revenue were taken out of the Court's reach. Statement 4 is incorrect: appeals from the Provincial Courts lay to the Governor-General-in-Council, not the Supreme Court. So 1, 2 and 3 only.
w: '1, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct
'2, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct
'1 and 2 only' leaves out statement 3, which is correct

questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the 1784 measure that created double government:

1. The Board of Control was set up to manage the commercial affairs of the Company.
2. The Court of Directors continued to manage the commercial affairs of the Company.
3. From 1784 the Company's holdings in India were officially described as 'British possessions in India' for the first time.
4. The Governor-General's Council was reduced from four members to three, counting the commander-in-chief.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: the Court of Directors kept the commercial affairs; the Board of Control managed the political affairs. Statement 2 is correct: this is one half of the double government. Statement 3 is correct: this marks the assertion of Crown claim over the territories. Statement 4 is correct: the size of the council was cut.
w: '1, 2 and 4 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct
'2 and 4 only' leaves out statement 3, which is correct
'1, 2 and 3 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 4, which is correct

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

1. The Board of Control created in 1784 had six members, including senior ministers such as the Chancellor of the Exchequer.
2. Under Pitt's India Act the Governor-General's Council was enlarged from four members to six.
3. Pitt's India Act placed the Company under strong government control, almost like a department of government.
4. The members of the Board of Control were nominated by the Court of Directors.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: senior British ministers sat on the Board. Statement 2 is incorrect: the Act reduced the Council from four members to three, counting the commander-in-chief. Statement 3 is correct: the Company became a controlled body. Statement 4 is incorrect: the Board represented the British Government and its senior members were ministers, not nominees of the Directors.
w: '1 and 4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct
'1, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect
'1 only' leaves out statement 3, which is correct

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Regulating Act of 1773:

1. The Executive Council assisting the Governor-General of Bengal had four members.
2. A separate legislative council was created for Bengal.
3. The Court of Directors was required to report to the British Government on the Company's revenue, civil and military affairs.
4. Warren Hastings was the first Governor-General of Bengal.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is incorrect: the Act created no separate legislative council; legislative work was separated from executive work only by the Charter Act of 1853. Statement 3 is correct:(reporting duty of the Court of Directors). Statement 4 is correct. So exactly 3 are correct.
w: 'Only one' miscounts: exactly 3 of the statements are correct.
'Only two' miscounts: exactly 3 of the statements are correct.
'All four' miscounts: exactly 3 of the statements are correct.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

1. Regulations for the Provincial Courts and Councils could be framed by the Governor-General-in-Council after the 1781 amendment.
2. The Amending Act of 1781 required the Supreme Court to apply one uniform English law to all inhabitants of Calcutta.
3. The Board of Control created in 1784 was composed of members drawn from the Court of Directors.
4. The Court of Directors was required by the 1773 Act to report on the Company's affairs.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: this is among its provisions. Statement 2 is incorrect: the Court had to administer the personal law of the defendants, Hindu law for Hindus and Muslim law for Muslims. Statement 3 is incorrect: it included senior British ministers. Statement 4 is correct: reporting duty. So exactly 2 are correct.
w: 'None' miscounts: exactly 2 of the statements are correct.
'Only one' miscounts: exactly 2 of the statements are correct.
'Only three' miscounts: exactly 2 of the statements are correct.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

1. The Company acquired the Diwani of Bengal, Bihar and Odisha in 1757, the year of Plassey.
2. The Regulating Act of 1773 allowed Company servants to accept presents from the natives if they were reported to the Directors.
3. Indian constitutional development is divided into the Company Rule (1773-1858) and the Crown Rule (1858-1947).
4. The East India Company received its charter from Queen Elizabeth I in 1608, the year in which the British first came to India.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: the Diwani was obtained in 1765 after Buxar, not in 1757. Statement 2 is incorrect: the Act prohibited private trade and the acceptance of presents or bribes. Statement 3 is correct: this two-phase division is the framework of the whole chapter. Statement 4 is incorrect: the charter of Queen Elizabeth I dates from 1600; 1608 is the year the British came to India as traders. So exactly 1 is correct.
w: 'Only two' miscounts: exactly 1 of the statements is correct.
'Only three' miscounts: exactly 1 of the statements is correct.
'None' miscounts: exactly 1 of the statements is correct.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

Statement-I: The Regulating Act of 1773 is regarded as having laid the foundations of central administration in India.
Statement-II: The Act made the Governors of Bombay and Madras presidencies subordinate to the Governor-General of Bengal, whereas the three presidencies had earlier been independent of one another.

Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
questions.a: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Statement-I is correct: the Regulating Act of 1773 is regarded as having laid the foundations of central administration in India. Statement-II is correct: making the Governors of Bombay and Madras subordinate to the Governor-General of Bengal was the concrete step that centralised authority. Statement-II gives the concrete provision which created a central authority and so explains Statement-I.
w: Rejected: II does explain I (Statement-II gives the concrete provision which created a central authority and so explains Statement-I).
Rejected: Statement-II is correct, since the Act did make the Bombay and Madras Governors subordinate to the Governor-General of Bengal.
Rejected: Statement-I is correct, since the 1773 Act is regarded as the foundation of central administration.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

Statement-I: Pitt's India Act of 1784 placed the Company under strong government control, almost like a government department.
Statement-II: The Act left the Court of Directors in charge of both the commercial and the political affairs of the Company.

Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
questions.a: Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
o: Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Statement-I is correct: the Board of Control supervised political affairs, while the Court of Directors kept commercial affairs. Statement-II is incorrect: the Court of Directors was left with commercial affairs only; political affairs went to the Board of Control.
w: Rejected: both are not correct (Statement-II is incorrect).
Rejected: both are not correct (Statement-II is incorrect).
Rejected: Statement-I is correct (the Board of Control supervised political affairs, while the Court of Directors kept commercial affairs).

questions.q:
Match each event in List-I with what it brought about in List-II.

List-I
A. Grant of Diwani (1765)
B. Regulating Act of 1773
C. Amending Act of 1781
D. The India Act piloted by Pitt in 1784

List-II
1. Appeals from Provincial Courts to the Governor-General-in-Council
2. Rights over revenue and civil justice in Bengal, Bihar and Odisha
3. Supreme Court at Calcutta, established in 1774
4. Board of Control for political affairs
questions.e: A-2: the Diwani gave revenue and civil-justice rights. B-3: the Regulating Act provided for the Supreme Court at Calcutta, established in 1774. C-1: the 1781 Act sent appeals from Provincial Courts to the Governor-General-in-Council. D-4: Pitt's Act created the Board of Control.
w: A and B, and C and D, are interchanged.
B and C are interchanged: the Supreme Court is a 1773 creation and the appeals rule is of 1781.
A and D are interchanged: Diwani concerned revenue; the Board of Control is of 1784.

concepts.name: Acts of 1786-1853: Charter Acts and Governors-General
concepts.description: The Act of 1786 and the Charter Acts of 1793, 1813, 1833 and 1853, with the Governors-General of the Company period.
concepts.idea: The Charter Acts progressively ended the Company's commerce, centralised power and then separated legislation from administration.
concepts.rule: The Act of 1786 gave Cornwallis the overriding power and the post of Commander-in-Chief. The Charter Act 1793 extended the monopoly by 20 years and the overriding power to all later heads. The 1813 Act ended the monopoly in India (tea and China trade continued), allowed missionaries and provided for western education. The 1833 Act made Bentinck the first Governor-General of India, centralised legislation, ended the Company's commerce and added a Law Member. The 1853 Act fixed no term, separated legislative from executive functions, added six legislative members and opened the civil service to competition.
concepts.example: Under the 1853 Act, Parliament could end the Company's rule at any time.

questions.q: Lord Cornwallis accepted the post of Governor-General of Bengal in 1786 only after two demands were met. The measure enacted to meet them gave him
questions.a: authority to overrule his council in exceptional cases together with command of the army
o: authority to overrule his council in exceptional cases together with command of the army
power to appoint the judges of the Supreme Court and to sit as a member of the Board of Control in London
exclusive legislative power over Bombay and Madras together with the right to nominate Directors of the Company
control of the Company's revenues in Bengal and the right to issue ordinances
questions.e: Cornwallis, appointed in 1786, demanded power to override his council in special cases and to be Commander-in-Chief; the Act of 1786 gave both.
w: The Supreme Court judges and the Board of Control were not part of the demands.
Exclusive legislative power over the other presidencies is a feature of the Charter Act of 1833, not of the Act of 1786.
Neither revenue control nor ordinance power was the subject of the 1786 Act; ordinance power came in 1861.

questions.q: The Charter Act of 1813 ended the Company's trade monopoly in India and opened Indian trade to all British merchants. The monopoly which it continued was over
questions.a: trade in tea and trade with China
o: trade in tea and trade with China
trade in opium and trade in salt in Bengal
trade in cotton goods and spices with Europe
trade in tea and trade with the Dutch settlements
questions.e: The 1813 Act abolished the Company's trade monopoly in India (open to all British merchants) but kept the monopoly of trade in tea and trade with China. This too was ended in 1833.
w: Opium and salt are not named; the continuing monopoly was tea and China trade.
Cotton and spices are not the monopolies continued by the 1813 Act.
Only the China trade, not trade with Dutch settlements, was retained along with tea.

questions.q: The Charter Act of 1833 vested in the Governor-General of Bengal all civil and military powers over the entire territorial area held by the British in India. The first person to hold this enlarged office, as Governor-General of India, was
questions.e: Bentinck was Governor-General when the 1833 Act made the office Governor-General of India and was its first holder.
w: Warren Hastings was the first Governor-General of Bengal under the Regulating Act of 1773.
Cornwallis was Governor-General of Bengal from 1786, long before the 1833 Act.
Dalhousie served 1848-56, after the Governor-General of India office had been created.

questions.q: Compared with the earlier Charter Acts, the Charter Act of 1853 is regarded as a landmark in the Company's rule mainly because it
questions.a: did not fix any period for the Company's rule, so Parliament could end it at any time
o: did not fix any period for the Company's rule, so Parliament could end it at any time
extended the Company's rule for a further twenty years, but placed it under the Crown's authority for the first time
ended the Company's rule and placed the Indian territories directly under the Crown with a Viceroy
restored the Company's trade monopoly in tea and China for a further twenty years
questions.e: The 1853 Act allowed the Company to retain possession of Indian territories on trust for the Crown without specifying any period, signalling Parliament could terminate its rule at will.
w: The earlier Charters fixed periods of twenty years; the 1853 Act fixed none.
The Crown assumed direct rule through the Government of India Act of 1858, not the Charter Act of 1853.
The China trade monopoly had been abolished in 1833; it was not restored.

questions.q: An association exists between a Governor-General and a policy, as in the case of Lord Dalhousie. Which one of the following correctly associates him?
questions.a: Doctrine of Lapse, annexations, and the introduction of railways and the telegraph
o: Doctrine of Lapse, annexations, and the introduction of railways and the telegraph
Subsidiary Alliance, the defeat of the Marathas and the expansion of control over the Indian princes
Abolition of sati, educational reforms and the beginning of the Indian Law Commission
Permanent Settlement of land revenue in Bengal and reforms in the civil service
questions.e: Dalhousie (1848-56) is associated with the Doctrine of Lapse, annexations, railways and the telegraph.
w: The Subsidiary Alliance is associated with Lord Wellesley.
Abolition of sati and educational reforms is associated with Lord William Bentinck.
The Permanent Settlement is associated with Lord Cornwallis.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Charter Act of 1793:

1. The salaries of the Board of Control and its staff were to be paid from British revenues.
2. The Company's trade monopoly in India was extended by a further twenty years.
3. The overriding power given to Cornwallis over his council was extended to all future Governors-General and Governors of Presidencies.
4. The Commander-in-Chief was not to be a member of the Governor-General's council unless specially appointed to it.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: they were henceforth to be paid out of Indian revenues. Statement 2 is correct: monopoly extension of twenty years. Statement 3 is correct: the special power became general. Statement 4 is correct: this restricted automatic membership.
w: '1, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct
'2 and 4 only' leaves out statement 3, which is correct
'3 and 4 only' leaves out statement 2, which is correct

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Charter Act of 1813:

1. It provided for the spread of western education in British India, and is recorded to have earmarked a sum of Rs 1 lakh a year for it.
2. It allowed Christian missionaries to come to India.
3. Local governments in India received the power to levy taxes on persons and to penalise non-payment.
4. The Company's Indian territories were declared to be held in trust for His Majesty, his heirs and successors.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: education provision. Statement 2 is correct: missionaries allowed. Statement 3 is correct: taxation power. Statement 4 is incorrect: this 'in trust' language is attributed to the Charter Act of 1833; the 1813 Act asserted the sovereignty of the Crown.
w: '1, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct
'1 and 3 only' leaves out statement 2, which is correct
'1, 2 and 4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Charter Act of 1813:

concepts.name: Crown rule: the Acts of 1858, 1861, 1892 and 1909
concepts.description: The Government of India Act 1858 and the Indian Councils Acts of 1861, 1892 and 1909.
concepts.idea: After 1857 the Crown ruled directly, and three Councils Acts widened Indian association in law-making, ending with separate electorates in 1909.
concepts.rule: The 1858 Act abolished the Company and the double government, created the Secretary of State with a 15-member Council of India and made the Governor-General the Viceroy (Canning). The 1861 Act nominated Indians, restored legislative powers to Bombay and Madras, recognised the portfolio system and allowed six-month ordinances. The 1892 Act allowed discussion of the budget and questions but no vote, with indirect representation. The 1909 Act (Morley-Minto) enlarged the Central council from 16 to 60, allowed non-official majorities in provinces and gave Muslims separate electorates.
concepts.example: Lord Minto is called the Father of the Communal Electorate.

o: a 15-member Council of India, which was an advisory body
a 12-member Board of Control, which supervised him on behalf of Parliament
an 18-member Court of Directors, which shared his powers over Indian finance
a 6-member Executive Council in London that could overrule his decisions
questions.e: The Secretary of State, with complete control over Indian administration, finance and policy, was assisted by a 15-member advisory Council of India.
w: The Board of Control was abolished by the 1858 Act.
The Court of Directors was abolished by the 1858 Act (and had been reduced to 18 by 1853).
The Council of India was advisory; it could not overrule the Secretary of State.

questions.q: The 'portfolio' system under which a member of the Viceroy's council was put in charge of one or more departments and could issue final orders on behalf of the council for them was, with respect to the Indian Councils Act of 1861,
questions.a: introduced earlier by Lord Canning in 1859 and given recognition by the Act
o: introduced earlier by Lord Canning in 1859 and given recognition by the Act
introduced by the Act itself, for the first time, in 1861, and confined to the Viceroy's council
introduced by Lord Dalhousie in 1853 and abolished by the Act as a centralising device
introduced by the Act of 1909 as part of the Morley-Minto Reforms, with Indian members in charge
questions.e: The 1861 Act gave recognition to the portfolio system introduced by Lord Canning in 1859.
w: The Act gave recognition to a system already introduced by Canning in 1859; it did not introduce it.
Dalhousie did not introduce the system, and the Act recognised it rather than abolishing it.
The system was in place decades before 1909.

questions.q: Under the Indian Councils Act of 1892 the legislative councils were allowed to
questions.a: discuss the budget and address questions to the executive, but not vote on the budget
o: discuss the budget and address questions to the executive, but not vote on the budget
vote on the budget and ask supplementary questions with six days' notice to the executive

discuss the budget and enact it without the Governor-General's assent
questions.e: The 1892 Act allowed discussion of the budget and questions (six days' notice; no supplementary questions); councils could recommend changes but not vote; the Governor-General's approval was needed for laws. Supplementary questions and resolutions on the budget were allowed in 1909.
w: Councils could not vote on the budget under the 1892 Act.
Resolutions on the budget and supplementary questions came with the Act of 1909, and the 1892 councils never voted on demands for grants.
Any law passed still required the approval of the Governor-General.

concepts.name: Acts of 1919, 1935 and 1947
concepts.description: The Government of India Act 1919, the Communal Award and Poona Pact, the Government of India Act 1935 and the Indian Independence Act 1947.
concepts.idea: From dyarchy in the provinces to provincial autonomy and finally to independent dominions, with the Communal Award and Poona Pact in between.
concepts.rule: The 1919 Act (in force 1921) introduced dyarchy in the provinces, a bicameral Centre and a High Commissioner. The Communal Award (1932) extended separate electorates to the Depressed Classes; the Poona Pact replaced them with reserved seats in a joint electorate. The 1935 Act (321 Sections, 10 Schedules) proposed a federation that never came into being, had three lists with 59, 54 and 36 items, abolished provincial dyarchy and set up the Federal Court in 1937. The 1947 Act ended British rule and created two dominions from 15 August 1947.
concepts.example: The central dyarchy under the 1935 Act never came into operation.

The High Commissioner took over only some of the Secretary of State's functions, not provincial reserved subjects.

questions.q:

questions.e: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is correct. Statement 3 is incorrect: they could repeal any British Act, including the Independence Act itself. w: '1, 2 and 3 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 4, which is correct

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

Statement-I: The dyarchy introduced in the provinces by the Act of 1919 was largely unsuccessful.
Statement-II: The Simon Commission, appointed in November 1927 to report on the working of the 1919 Act, had only British members.

Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
questions.a: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Statement-I is correct: the dyarchy experiment under the Act of 1919 was largely unsuccessful. Statement-II is correct: all seven members of the Simon Commission (appointed November 1927 to review the working of the 1919 Act) were British. II concerns who sat on the review commission; it does not state why the dyarchy failed and so does not explain Statement-I.
w: Rejected: II does not explain I (the composition of a later review commission does not state why dyarchy failed).
Rejected: Statement-II is correct, since the Simon Commission had only British members.
Rejected: Statement-I is correct, since dyarchy under the 1919 Act was largely unsuccessful.
tr: Review commission is not a cause
